title: Annual Leave Policy
body:
The Annual Leave Policy establishes the framework for annual leave entitlements, procedures, and responsibilities, ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law while balancing employee well-being and operational continuity. This policy applies to all full-time employees of inmind.ai who have completed the required period of continuous service.

### Annual Leave Entitlement
Employees are entitled to a minimum of 15 working days of paid annual leave upon completing one year of uninterrupted service, as stipulated by Lebanese Labour Law. For employees who have not yet completed one year of service, annual leave entitlement will be calculated on a pro-rata basis, with leave accrued at the rate of 1.25 days per month worked. Leave is calculated based on the calendar year, starting January 1st and ending December 31st. Part-time employees and contractual workers are not eligible for annual leave under this policy unless explicitly stated in their employment contracts.

### Procedures for Requesting Leave
1. **Submission of Leave Requests**: Employees must submit a written leave request through the company’s designated HR management system or via email to their direct supervisor. The request must specify the intended dates of leave and should be submitted at least two (2) weeks in advance.
2. **Approval Process**: The direct supervisor will review the leave request, taking into account operational requirements, workload distribution, and team availability. Once reviewed, the supervisor will forward the request to the HR department for final approval.
3. **Notification of Approval/Decline**: Employees will receive written confirmation of their leave approval or a valid explanation for denial within five (5) working days of submitting their request.
4. **Documentation**: Approved leave requests will be documented in the employee’s records to ensure accurate tracking of leave balances.

### Scheduling and Usage of Leave
- Employees are encouraged to plan their leave in coordination with their team to minimize disruption to business operations.
- Leave may be taken in full or in increments of at least one (1) working day, unless otherwise approved by management.
- Employees are required to utilize their annual leave within the same calendar year. Unused leave days will be forfeited unless exceptional circumstances apply.

### Carryover and Forfeiture of Leave
In alignment with company policy, unused leave days cannot be carried over to the following calendar year unless written approval is granted by management. Such approval will only be considered under exceptional circumstances, such as the employee being unable to take leave due to a critical business need or personal emergencies. Any carryover leave must be used within the first quarter (January 1 to March 31) of the subsequent year. Failure to do so will result in the forfeiture of unused leave days.

### Exceptions to Policy
1. **Probationary Employees**: Employees on probation are not eligible to take annual leave. However, they will begin accruing leave from their start date, and the accrued balance will be available upon successful completion of the probationary period.
2. **Unforeseen Circumstances**: In cases of unforeseen personal emergencies, employees may request annual leave on short notice. Such requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to approval by management.
3. **Overlapping Leave Requests**: If multiple employees within the same team submit overlapping leave requests, priority will be determined based on the order of submission, operational needs, and, where applicable, seniority.

### Employee Responsibilities
Employees are responsible for:
- Planning and submitting leave requests in a timely manner.
- Ensuring that their duties are adequately delegated or completed before the start of their leave.
- Providing accurate and honest information regarding leave requests.
- Returning to work on the agreed-upon date and resuming duties promptly.

### Employer Responsibilities
The company is committed to:
- Ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law regarding annual leave entitlements.
- Reviewing and responding to leave requests within a reasonable timeframe.
- Balancing employee well-being with business operational needs.
- Providing a transparent and accessible system for tracking and managing leave balances.

### Compliance and Disciplinary Measures
Employees are required to adhere strictly to the procedures and guidelines outlined in this policy. Abuse of leave privileges, such as submitting fraudulent leave requests or failing to return to work as scheduled, will result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment, as per the company’s disciplinary policy.

### Compliance with Lebanese Labour Law
This policy has been developed in accordance with the provisions of Lebanese Labour Law, which mandates a minimum of 15 days of annual leave for employees who have completed one year of service. Any updates to relevant legislation will be incorporated into this policy to ensure continued compliance.

### Review and Amendments
This policy will be reviewed annually by the HR department to ensure alignment with legal requirements and organizational needs. Any amendments will be communicated to all employees in a timely manner.

By adhering to this policy, inmind.ai aims to foster a balanced workplace environment where employees are encouraged to take time off to recharge, while ensuring that business continuity is maintained.

title: Code of Conduct Policy
body:
The Code of Conduct Policy establishes clear expectations regarding professional behavior, ethical standards, and compliance with company rules and applicable Lebanese labor laws. This policy aims to ensure a respectful, inclusive, and legally compliant workplace environment. All employees of inmind.ai are required to familiarize themselves with this policy and uphold its principles as part of their professional responsibilities. Any violations of this policy will be addressed promptly and appropriately to maintain the integrity of the organization and its operations.

**1. Standard of Professional Behavior**
Employees are expected to demonstrate integrity, respect, and accountability in all aspects of their professional conduct. This includes:
- Treating colleagues, clients, and external stakeholders with dignity and respect.
- Refraining from discriminatory, harassing, or bullying behavior based on race, gender, religion, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic as per Lebanese labor law.
- Collaborating effectively and respectfully with team members to achieve organizational goals.

**2. Compliance with Company Rules and Legal Requirements**
Employees must adhere to all corporate policies, operational procedures, and applicable Lebanese labor regulations. The company will provide regular training and updates on relevant laws to ensure awareness and compliance. Noncompliance, including engaging in illegal activities or violating company rules, will be subject to disciplinary action.

**3. Confidentiality and Data Protection**
Maintaining confidentiality is paramount. Employees must:
- Safeguard sensitive company information, including trade secrets, financial data, client information, and intellectual property.
- Refrain from disclosing confidential information to unauthorized individuals or external entities, even after the termination of their employment.
- Adhere to applicable data protection laws, such as the Lebanese Electronic Transactions and Personal Data Law (Law No. 81 of 2018).

Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information will result in disciplinary action, including possible termination and legal recourse.

**4. Use of Company Assets**
Employees are entrusted with company resources, including computers, software, and office supplies, and must use them responsibly. Misuse, including theft, fraud, or unauthorized personal use, will not be tolerated. Employees are responsible for:
- Ensuring proper use and care of company assets.
- Reporting any damage, loss, or misuse to their immediate supervisor.

**5. Workplace Attire and Professional Appearance**
Employees are required to wear appropriate attire that reflects professionalism and aligns with the company’s image. Specific guidelines include:
- Business casual dress code for regular workdays unless otherwise specified.
- Adherence to safety and protective clothing requirements, where applicable.
- Exceptions may be made for religious or cultural attire consistent with the principles of inclusivity.

**6. Conflict of Interest**
Employees must avoid conflicts of interest that could compromise the company’s operations or reputation. If a potential conflict arises, employees are required to:
- Disclose the matter in writing to their manager or the HR department immediately.
- Refrain from participating in decisions or activities that may present a conflict until the matter is resolved.

Examples of conflicts of interest include, but are not limited to:
- Engaging in outside employment or business activities that compete with the company.
- Accepting gifts or favors from clients or vendors that could influence decisions.

**7. Reporting Violations**
The company encourages employees to report any violations of this policy, whether they involve themselves, colleagues, or management. Reporting channels include:
- Direct reporting to immediate supervisors.
- Filing a formal complaint with the HR department.
- Utilizing the confidential whistleblower hotline, where anonymity is guaranteed.

All reports will be treated seriously and investigated promptly. Retaliation against individuals who report violations in good faith is strictly prohibited and will be subject to disciplinary action.

**8. Disciplinary Actions**
Violations of the Code of Conduct Policy will result in corrective measures, which may include the following, depending on the severity and nature of the breach:
- Verbal or written warnings.
- Suspension without pay.
- Termination of employment.
- Legal action, where necessary, in accordance with Lebanese labor laws.

Disciplinary actions will be determined by management in consultation with the HR department and will be communicated to the employee in writing.

**9. Responsibilities**
- **Employee Responsibilities:** Employees are responsible for understanding and adhering to the Code of Conduct Policy. They must participate in training sessions and seek clarification from HR if any aspect of the policy is unclear.
- **Employer Responsibilities:** The company is responsible for providing a safe and inclusive work environment, offering training on ethical practices, and ensuring that all employees are aware of their rights and responsibilities under this policy. The company will also ensure that all reports of misconduct are addressed fairly and confidentially.

**10. Exceptions and Limitations**
Certain provisions of this policy may have exceptions, such as:
- Workplace attire requirements may be adjusted based on specific job roles or cultural/religious needs.
- Instances of conflict of interest may be resolved through predefined agreements, provided they do not harm the company’s interests.

Any requested exception must be formally submitted to the HR department for review and approval. Exceptions will be granted on a case-by-case basis, and decisions will be documented.

**11. Compliance and Review**
This policy is subject to periodic review to ensure alignment with Lebanese labor laws and evolving organizational needs. Employees will be notified of any updates or changes to the policy. Failure to comply with this policy may result in disciplinary action, as outlined above.

By adhering to this Code of Conduct Policy, employees contribute to a professional, ethical, and harmonious workplace that supports the company’s mission and values.

title: Remote Work Policy
body:
The Remote Work Policy establishes a framework for eligible employees to perform their duties from home or other remote locations, ensuring that such arrangements align with the company’s operational needs, employee performance standards, and applicable provisions under Lebanese Labour Law. This policy is designed to provide flexibility while maintaining accountability, productivity, and compliance with legal and organizational requirements.

**Eligibility Criteria**
Remote work arrangements are not an automatic right and will be granted at the discretion of management. Eligibility is determined based on the following criteria:
1. **Job Requirements**: The role must be suitable for remote execution without compromising the quality of work or team collaboration. Positions that require a high degree of in-person interaction, such as those in facilities management or on-site IT support, may not qualify for remote work.
2. **Employee Performance**: Employees must have demonstrated a consistent level of productivity, reliability, and accountability in their current role. Employees on Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs) or those with documented instances of misconduct may not be eligible.
3. **Operational Feasibility**: Management will evaluate the impact of remote work on team dynamics, communication, and overall business operations before approving any arrangement.
4. **Trial Period**: New employees must complete a mandatory probation period of three months before becoming eligible for remote work, unless otherwise specified in their employment contract.

**Procedure to Request Remote Work**
1. **Submission of Request**: Employees must submit a formal written request for remote work to their immediate supervisor, outlining the reasons for the request and how they will meet job expectations while working remotely.
2. **Manager Review**: Supervisors will assess the request against the eligibility criteria and discuss it with the employee to address any concerns or clarify expectations.
3. **Approval Process**: Approved requests will be escalated to the department head and the HR department for final confirmation. Employees will be notified of the decision within five business days of submitting their request.
4. **Remote Work Agreement**: Employees whose requests are approved must sign a Remote Work Agreement, which outlines their obligations, including but not limited to:
   - Defined working hours.
   - Availability for communication during working hours.
   - Productivity and performance expectations.
   - Data security and confidentiality requirements.

**Employee Responsibilities**
1. **Work Environment**: Remote employees must establish and maintain a professional and distraction-free work environment. This includes having an ergonomic workspace and ensuring minimal disruptions during working hours.
2. **Data Security**: Employees are required to adhere to company IT policies, including the secure use of company-issued devices, strong password management, and compliance with data protection regulations under Lebanese law.
3. **Resources**: Unless explicitly agreed otherwise, employees are responsible for ensuring adequate internet connectivity and other necessary resources to perform their tasks effectively.
4. **Communication**: Employees must remain reachable via email, phone, or other designated communication platforms during agreed working hours. Participation in virtual meetings, as scheduled by the company, is mandatory.

**Employer Responsibilities**
1. **Provision of Equipment**: The company may provide essential equipment (e.g., laptops, software licenses) for remote work, subject to an inventory agreement signed by the employee.
2. **Performance Monitoring**: Supervisors are responsible for monitoring the performance of remote employees and providing regular feedback. Performance reviews will include an evaluation of remote work outcomes, such as meeting deadlines, maintaining productivity, and contributing to team goals.
3. **Support and Training**: The company will offer training sessions on remote work best practices and the use of digital communication tools to ensure employees are well-equipped for remote work.

**Timelines for Remote Work Arrangements**
1. Approved remote work arrangements may be temporary or long-term, depending on the nature of the request and business needs. The duration of the arrangement will be specified in the Remote Work Agreement.
2. Temporary arrangements will be reviewed after an initial trial period of three months, with the possibility of extension based on performance and operational impact.
3. Long-term arrangements will be reviewed annually as part of the employee’s performance evaluation.

**Exceptions and Special Circumstances**
1. **Emergency Remote Work**: In cases of emergencies (e.g., natural disasters, pandemics, or political unrest), management may impose mandatory remote work for all eligible employees. In such instances, the company will provide additional support and guidance to ensure business continuity.
2. **Medical Accommodation**: Employees requiring remote work as a reasonable accommodation for medical reasons must provide a valid medical certificate. Such requests will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis in accordance with Lebanese Labour Law and company policies.
3. **Employee Relocation**: Employees wishing to work remotely from a different country or jurisdiction must obtain prior approval from management and HR. Such arrangements will be subject to local employment laws, tax implications, and the company's operational capacity to support cross-border remote work.

**Termination or Modification of Remote Work Arrangements**
1. The company reserves the right to modify or terminate remote work arrangements if they negatively impact performance, team collaboration, or overall business operations. Employees will be provided with a minimum of 14 days’ notice before any such change, except in cases of misconduct or urgent business needs.
2. Employees may request to terminate their remote work arrangement and return to on-site work by providing written notice to their supervisor at least 14 days in advance.

**Compliance and Disciplinary Measures**
1. Employees found to be in breach of the Remote Work Agreement, including but not limited to instances of data breaches, misuse of company equipment, or non-compliance with working hours, may face disciplinary action in accordance with the company’s Code of Conduct and Lebanese Labour Law.
2. Regular audits may be conducted to ensure compliance with the policy, including the proper use of company-provided equipment and adherence to performance standards.

This policy serves to foster a flexible and productive work environment while safeguarding the company’s operational integrity and ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law.

title: Employee Termination Policy
body:
The Employee Termination Policy sets forth the guidelines, procedures, and conditions under which employment may be terminated at Inmind.ai, in strict adherence to Lebanese Labour Law. This policy ensures that terminations are conducted fairly, transparently, and in compliance with all legal obligations to protect the rights of both the company and its employees. Termination of employment can occur under the following circumstances: resignation, redundancy, misconduct, or performance-related issues. The specific procedures, eligibility criteria, timelines, exceptions, and responsibilities for each type of termination are outlined below. 

1. **Resignation**:
Employees who choose to resign from their position must provide formal written notice to the company, as stipulated in their employment contract. The notice period will typically range from one to three months, depending on the employee's role, seniority, and contract terms. During the notice period, the employee is expected to fulfill all work-related responsibilities and assist in the smooth transition of their duties. Failure to adhere to the notice period may result in forfeiture of certain benefits, such as end-of-service indemnities, unless the employee can demonstrate exceptional circumstances (e.g., medical emergencies or relocation).

**Employee Responsibilities**:
- Submit a signed resignation letter to the HR department, specifying the intended last working day.
- Cooperate with management to ensure a proper handover of responsibilities.
- Return all company property, including equipment, documents, and access credentials, before the final day of employment.

**Employer Responsibilities**:
- Acknowledge receipt of the resignation letter in writing.
- Facilitate the handover process to minimize disruption to business operations.
- Process final settlements, including any outstanding salary, unused leave, and end-of-service indemnity, within a maximum of 30 days from the employee's last working day.

2. **Redundancy**:
Employment may be terminated due to redundancy if the company undergoes structural changes, financial challenges, or operational downsizing. In such cases, the company will follow a transparent process to identify affected roles and provide employees with adequate notice and compensation as required by Lebanese Labour Law.

**Eligibility Criteria**:
- Redundancy will only apply to roles that are no longer required or viable due to business needs.
- Employees with longer tenures and higher contributions may be prioritized for retention, where applicable.

**Procedures**:
- A minimum notice period of one month will be provided to affected employees, or as otherwise stipulated in their employment contracts.
- Eligible employees will receive severance pay calculated based on their years of service, in accordance with Article 50 of the Lebanese Labour Law.
- Employees will be offered support services, such as outplacement assistance, where feasible.

**Employer Responsibilities**:
- Provide written notification of redundancy, specifying reasons and effective dates.
- Ensure compliance with legal severance requirements and timely processing of payments.
- Communicate openly and transparently to address employee concerns.

3. **Misconduct**:
Termination due to misconduct will only occur following a thorough investigation and due process to ensure fairness. Misconduct may include, but is not limited to, theft, harassment, violence, or willful violation of company policies.

**Procedures**:
- The company will initiate a formal investigation upon receiving a complaint or identifying potential misconduct.
- The employee in question will be notified in writing and given an opportunity to respond to the allegations.
- A disciplinary hearing may be conducted to review evidence and statements from all parties involved.
- A final decision will be communicated to the employee in writing, along with the rationale for termination if applicable.

**Exceptions**:
- Immediate termination without notice may occur in cases of gross misconduct, as defined under Article 74 of the Lebanese Labour Law.

**Employee Responsibilities**:
- Provide truthful information during the investigation process.
- Abide by company policies and the terms of their employment contract.

**Employer Responsibilities**:
- Conduct a fair, impartial, and confidential investigation.
- Maintain detailed documentation of the investigation process and decisions made.
- Ensure compliance with legal requirements for termination due to misconduct.

4. **Performance-Related Termination**:
Termination due to performance issues will only occur after the employee has been given adequate opportunities to improve. This includes documented feedback, performance evaluations, and the implementation of a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP).

**Procedures**:
- Supervisors will provide written warnings outlining specific performance concerns and expectations for improvement.
- If concerns persist, a PIP will be initiated, specifying measurable goals and a timeline for achieving them (typically 30 to 90 days).
- Regular check-ins will be scheduled to track progress and provide guidance.
- If performance remains unsatisfactory after the PIP period, termination may be initiated in accordance with the employee's contract and Lebanese Labour Law.

**Employee Responsibilities**:
- Actively participate in the PIP process and work towards achieving outlined goals.
- Seek clarification or support from supervisors if needed.

**Employer Responsibilities**:
- Provide clear, constructive feedback and support throughout the PIP process.
- Document all warnings, evaluations, and improvement plans.
- Ensure performance-related terminations are conducted fairly and in compliance with legal standards.

5. **Final Settlement and Return of Company Property**:
Upon termination, employees are required to return all company property, including laptops, access cards, and confidential documents. Final settlements, including unused leave balances, end-of-service indemnities, and any outstanding salary, will be processed within a maximum of 30 days from the official termination date.

**Compliance Notes**:
- The company strictly adheres to the provisions of the Lebanese Labour Law, including Articles 47-50, which govern notice periods, severance pay, and termination procedures.
- Employees and managers are encouraged to consult the HR department for clarification on any aspect of this policy.
- Non-compliance with this policy by either party may result in legal action or penalties as prescribed by law.

By adhering to this policy, Inmind.ai aims to maintain fairness, transparency, and legal compliance in all termination-related decisions and processes.

title: Workplace Benefits Policy
body:
The Workplace Benefits Policy is designed to outline the comprehensive range of benefits provided by inmind.ai to support the well-being, professional growth, and job satisfaction of its employees. This policy ensures compliance with Lebanese Labour Law while reflecting the company’s commitment to fostering a positive and supportive work environment. The following sections detail the specific benefits available, eligibility criteria, procedures to access benefits, timelines, exceptions, and both employee and employer responsibilities.

### 1. Health and Wellness Benefits
The company provides health insurance coverage to all eligible employees. This includes medical, dental, and vision benefits, ensuring employees have access to essential healthcare services. Specific provisions include:
- Coverage: The insurance plan covers hospitalization, outpatient services, dental care, and vision correction as per the terms of the insurance policy.
- Eligibility: Health insurance becomes available after the successful completion of the probation period (a standard period of three months unless otherwise specified in the employment contract).
- Enrollment: New employees must submit the required documentation, including a copy of their identification card and family status declaration (if dependents are included), within 15 days of completing their probation period.
- Dependents: Employees may add dependents (spouse and children) to their health insurance plan at their own expense, with costs deducted from their monthly salary.
- Exceptions: Part-time employees, freelancers, and consultants may not be eligible for company-sponsored health insurance.

### 2. Leave Entitlements
The company offers leave entitlements in accordance with Lebanese Labour Law and additional leave types to support employees' personal and professional needs. 
- **Annual Leave**: Employees are entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave after one year of continuous service. Leave requests must be submitted at least one month in advance through the HR portal and approved by the employee’s direct supervisor. Unused annual leave cannot be carried over to the following year unless pre-approved by HR for exceptional circumstances.
- **Sick Leave**: Employees are entitled to sick leave with pay as per Lebanese Labour Law, subject to submission of a medical report from a licensed physician. The maximum duration and pay structure adhere to legal provisions based on the employee’s tenure.
- **Maternity and Paternity Leave**: Female employees are entitled to 10 weeks of maternity leave with full pay, as per Lebanese Labour Law. Male employees are entitled to three continuous days of paternity leave with full pay. Requests must be submitted at least two months in advance, accompanied by relevant documentation, such as a medical certificate indicating the expected delivery date.
- **Other Leave Types**: Employees may request bereavement leave, marriage leave, or unpaid leave under specific circumstances. These requests are subject to approval by HR and management.

### 3. Financial and Workplace Benefits
In addition to statutory benefits, the company provides supplementary benefits to enhance employees' quality of life:
- **Transportation Allowances**: Employees are entitled to transportation allowances as mandated by Lebanese Labour Law. These are calculated based on the number of days worked each month.
- **Meal Vouchers**: Depending on the employee's role and work location, the company may provide meal vouchers to cover daily lunch expenses. Eligibility and the monthly voucher amount are determined by HR.
- **Performance-Based Bonuses**: The company may award bonuses at its discretion, based on individual and company performance. Bonuses are typically disbursed annually and subject to approval from senior management.

### 4. Professional Development Opportunities
To foster continuous learning and skill development, the company offers professional development benefits, including:
- **Training Programs**: Employees may attend internal or external training programs relevant to their role. Participation requires approval from the employee’s supervisor and HR.
- **Certifications**: The company may reimburse employees for certifications that enhance their professional skills and align with business needs. Reimbursement is subject to prior approval and submission of proof of completion and payment.
- **Tuition Reimbursement**: Employees pursuing higher education relevant to their job may apply for partial tuition reimbursement. Applications must include a detailed study plan, cost breakdown, and supervisor endorsement. Reimbursements are capped annually and subject to budget availability.

### 5. Eligibility and Conditions
- Full-time employees are eligible for all benefits outlined in this policy after the successful completion of their probation period.
- Part-time employees and consultants are eligible only for statutory benefits as per Lebanese Labour Law, unless otherwise specified in their contracts.
- Employees must comply with all company policies and submit required documentation within the specified timelines to access benefits.
- Misuse of benefits, such as falsifying medical reports or excessive absenteeism, will lead to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

### 6. Exceptions and Limitations
- The company reserves the right to amend or discontinue non-statutory benefits (e.g., meal vouchers or bonuses) based on operational needs, financial constraints, or legal changes.
- Employees on unpaid leave or extended absences may have certain benefits, such as health insurance, suspended temporarily unless otherwise agreed upon.
- In cases of force majeure or economic hardship, benefits may be temporarily adjusted to ensure business continuity.

### 7. Responsibilities
- **Employees**: Employees are responsible for understanding their entitlements, submitting required documentation within deadlines, and using benefits ethically and responsibly.
- **Employer**: The company is responsible for ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law, maintaining transparency in benefit administration, and communicating any changes to this policy in a timely manner.

### 8. Compliance and Review
The company is committed to full compliance with all applicable provisions of Lebanese Labour Law. This policy will be reviewed annually or as required to reflect changes in legal requirements, market standards, or company circumstances. Employees will be notified of any amendments to the benefits package through official communication channels.

This Workplace Benefits Policy is intended to attract, retain, and motivate employees by addressing their professional and personal needs while ensuring alignment with legal obligations and organizational values. By offering a robust benefits program, inmind.ai demonstrates its dedication to employee satisfaction and long-term success.

title: Working Hours Policy
body:
The Working Hours Policy establishes the guidelines and expectations for employees' work schedules, including regular working hours, overtime, and attendance, in full compliance with Lebanese Labour Law. This policy ensures operational efficiency, promotes fairness, and safeguards employees' rights to appropriate working conditions.

**1. Standard Working Hours:**
The standard working hours are fixed at 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week, excluding lunch and rest breaks. Employees are entitled to one full rest day per week, typically on Sundays unless otherwise stipulated in their employment contract or agreed upon with management. For roles requiring weekend work, an alternative rest day will be provided during the workweek. Employees must adhere to their assigned schedules and are expected to be punctual to ensure the smooth functioning of business operations.

**2. Attendance and Time Tracking:**
All employees are required to accurately record their working hours using the company's designated attendance tracking system. This may include biometric systems, manual attendance logs, or software solutions as determined by the management. Employees must report any discrepancies in their recorded hours to the Human Resources (HR) department within 24 hours of identifying the issue. Supervisors are responsible for reviewing attendance records regularly to ensure compliance and to address any irregularities promptly. 

**3. Overtime Work:**
Any work performed beyond the standard 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week is classified as overtime. Overtime is voluntary and must be pre-approved by the employee's direct supervisor. The approval process includes submitting a formal request at least 24 hours before the anticipated overtime, unless the overtime is required to address an urgent operational need. Compensation for overtime will be calculated in accordance with Lebanese Labour Law, which mandates payment at a rate of 1.5 times the employee's regular hourly wage for overtime hours. In cases where the overtime exceeds 12 hours in a single week, employees may also be entitled to additional rest days or compensatory time off, subject to management approval.

**4. Flexible Working Hours:**
The company recognizes the need for flexibility in certain roles and under specific circumstances. Flexible working hours may be granted to employees whose roles do not require strict adherence to a fixed schedule, such as remote workers or project-based employees. To request flexible hours, employees must submit a formal application to their supervisor and HR, outlining the reasons for the request and how they plan to maintain their productivity. Approval is subject to operational requirements, and the arrangement will be reviewed periodically to ensure its feasibility and alignment with company goals. 

**5. Rest Breaks:**
Employees are entitled to a daily lunch break of at least one continuous hour, as mandated by Lebanese Labour Law. Additional short breaks may be allocated based on the nature of work and department-specific policies. Breaks are not included in the calculation of standard working hours. Employees are encouraged to utilize their breaks to rest and recharge to maintain productivity and well-being.

**6. Exceptions to Standard Working Hours:**
Certain roles may require deviations from the standard working hours, such as night shifts, rotational schedules, or extended hours during peak operational periods. In such cases, employees will be notified in advance, and the company will ensure compliance with applicable laws regarding rest periods and compensation. Temporary changes in working hours due to business needs, such as project deadlines or emergencies, will be communicated at least 48 hours in advance whenever possible. Employees with personal obligations or health conditions that conflict with such changes may request accommodations, which will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

**7. Tardiness and Absenteeism:**
Employees are expected to report to work on time and adhere to their designated schedules. Tardiness or unexcused absences disrupt the workflow and may affect team productivity. Employees who are unable to report to work on time must inform their supervisor and HR as soon as possible, providing a valid reason and an estimated time of arrival. Repeated instances of tardiness or unexcused absenteeism will be addressed through the company’s disciplinary procedures, which may include verbal or written warnings, suspension, or termination in severe cases.

**8. Employer Responsibilities:**
The company is committed to ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law and providing fair and reasonable working conditions for all employees. This includes:
- Monitoring and enforcing adherence to standard working hours and overtime regulations.
- Maintaining accurate records of employee attendance and overtime work.
- Providing timely and accurate compensation for regular and overtime hours.
- Accommodating reasonable requests for flexible schedules or rest breaks within operational constraints.
- Communicating any changes to working hours or policies in a timely manner.

**9. Employee Responsibilities:**
Employees are expected to:
- Adhere to their designated working hours and report any anticipated delays to their supervisor.
- Accurately record their attendance and working hours in the approved system.
- Seek prior approval for overtime or flexible working arrangements.
- Utilize rest breaks responsibly to maintain productivity.
- Report any violations of this policy or concerns about working hours to HR for resolution.

**10. Compliance and Review:**
This policy is designed to comply fully with the provisions of Lebanese Labour Law. Any updates to the law will be reflected in this policy to ensure continued compliance. The HR department will conduct an annual review of the policy to assess its effectiveness and relevance. Employees found violating the provisions of this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination, depending on the severity of the violation.

By implementing this Working Hours Policy, the company aims to balance operational efficiency with employees' rights, promoting a fair, safe, and productive work environment for all.

title: Sick Leave Policy
body:
The Sick Leave Policy outlines the procedures, eligibility criteria, and responsibilities associated with taking leave due to illness or injury. This policy complies with Lebanese Labour Law and aims to support employee health while ensuring minimal disruption to business operations. 

**1. Eligibility Criteria:**
Employees who are unable to perform their work duties due to physical or mental illness or injury are eligible for sick leave. To qualify for paid sick leave, employees must meet the following conditions:
- Be a full-time employee of inmind.ai with a valid employment contract.
- Have completed at least three months of continuous service with the company.
- Submit a valid medical certificate within the required timeframe (described below).

Part-time and probationary employees may also request sick leave; however, their entitlement to paid sick leave will be assessed on a case-by-case basis and according to applicable Lebanese Labour Law.

**2. Sick Leave Entitlements:**
In compliance with Lebanese Labour Law, employees are entitled to up to 15 days of paid sick leave per calendar year, provided they submit valid medical documentation. The following terms apply:
- Paid sick leave is calculated based on the employee's most recent salary.
- Sick leave balances reset at the beginning of each calendar year and cannot be carried forward.
- Sick leave beyond the 15-day annual allowance may be granted as unpaid leave or additional paid leave at the discretion of management and on a case-by-case basis.

**3. Notification Procedures:**
Employees who are unable to report to work due to illness or injury must adhere to the following notification procedures:
- Notify the direct supervisor as soon as possible, preferably within one hour of the start of the workday.
- Provide an estimate of the expected duration of the absence.
- If the absence extends beyond three consecutive days, submit a valid medical certificate from a licensed healthcare provider.
- In cases of sudden illness or emergency, employees may designate a family member or representative to notify the company on their behalf.

**4. Documentation Requirements:**
To ensure compliance with company policies and Lebanese Labour Law, employees must provide proper documentation for all sick leave requests exceeding three consecutive days. Documentation must include:
- A medical certificate issued by a licensed physician or healthcare provider, clearly stating the nature of the illness or injury and the recommended period of absence.
- If requested by the company, additional documentation, such as medical test results or specialists' reports, may be required.
- All documentation must be submitted to the HR department within five business days of the absence start date.

**5. Exceptions and Special Circumstances:**
The company recognizes that certain situations may require additional flexibility. The following exceptions apply:
- In cases of prolonged illness or chronic medical conditions, additional paid or unpaid sick leave may be granted at the discretion of management.
- Employees who are hospitalized or require long-term treatment may be eligible for extended leave arrangements under the company's Leave Without Pay policy.
- Sick leave taken for the care of an immediate family member (e.g., spouse, child, or parent) will be considered on a case-by-case basis and may be deducted from the employee's annual leave balance if approved.
- Employees who are unable to provide medical documentation due to exceptional circumstances must communicate this to the HR department as soon as possible for further guidance.

**6. Abuse of Sick Leave Policy:**
Sick leave is intended to support the recovery and well-being of employees. Abuse or misuse of this policy is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action. Examples of abuse include:
- Submitting fraudulent or falsified medical certificates.
- Taking sick leave for reasons unrelated to health or well-being without prior approval.
- Excessive absenteeism without valid justification or documentation.

**7. Independent Medical Evaluation:**
The company reserves the right to request an independent medical evaluation in the following cases:
- Prolonged or frequent absences that raise concerns about the employee's ability to perform their duties.
- Situations where the validity of the medical documentation submitted by the employee is in question.
- Cases involving potential workplace-related injuries or illnesses.

The cost of the independent medical evaluation will be borne by the company, and the employee will be required to comply with the evaluation process.

**8. Employee Responsibilities:**
Employees are expected to:
- Notify their supervisor promptly in the event of illness or injury.
- Submit all required documentation in a timely manner.
- Avoid engaging in activities that may delay recovery or exacerbate their condition while on sick leave.
- Maintain open communication with their supervisor and the HR department regarding any updates on their health status or return-to-work plans.

**9. Employer Responsibilities:**
The company is committed to:
- Ensuring all employees are aware of their sick leave rights and responsibilities.
- Handling sick leave requests in a fair and consistent manner.
- Maintaining the confidentiality of employees' medical information, in compliance with applicable privacy laws.
- Providing reasonable accommodations for employees returning to work after a prolonged illness or injury.

**10. Compliance and Disciplinary Measures:**
To ensure compliance with this policy, the company will:
- Monitor sick leave usage and address any patterns of excessive or unexplained absenteeism.
- Conduct investigations in cases where fraudulent or falsified medical certificates are suspected.
- Apply disciplinary measures, up to and including termination, for employees found to be in violation of this policy.

**11. Review and Amendments:**
This policy is subject to periodic review to ensure adherence to Lebanese Labour Law and alignment with company objectives. Any amendments to the policy will be communicated to all employees in writing.

By adhering to this Sick Leave Policy, employees and management can work together to maintain a healthy and productive workplace while respecting the rights and obligations of all parties.

title: Disciplinary Action Policy
body:
The Disciplinary Action Policy outlines the procedures, eligibility criteria, timelines, and responsibilities for addressing employee misconduct or violations of company policies, ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law. This policy is designed to promote accountability, correct behavior, and maintain a professional work environment that aligns with organizational standards and legal requirements.

**Scope and Applicability**
This policy applies to all employees of inmind.ai, regardless of role or seniority. Disciplinary measures may be enforced for actions including, but not limited to, absenteeism, insubordination, harassment, theft, breach of confidentiality, unauthorized use of company resources, or any behavior that contravenes company policies or Lebanese Labour Law. This policy ensures all employees are treated fairly and respectfully during the disciplinary process.

**Eligibility Criteria**
Disciplinary action may be initiated if:
1. An employee violates company policies or procedures.
2. An act contravenes Lebanese Labour Law or workplace standards.
3. Misconduct disrupts the work environment or jeopardizes the safety of employees or company assets.
4. Repeated offenses occur, despite prior corrective measures.

Employees will not be subject to disciplinary action for issues unrelated to misconduct, such as performance concerns, unless such performance directly violates company standards or policies.

**Procedures**
The disciplinary process consists of several stages to ensure transparency and fairness:
1. **Incident Reporting**: All incidents of alleged misconduct must be reported by the concerned party (manager, colleague, or witness) to the Human Resources (HR) department within five business days of the occurrence or discovery.
2. **Preliminary Review**: HR will conduct a preliminary review within three business days to determine whether the case warrants formal investigation. If the matter is minor or resolvable informally, HR may issue guidance or coaching without initiating formal disciplinary action.
3. **Formal Investigation**: For serious allegations, HR will initiate a formal investigation within five business days. This includes collecting evidence, interviewing relevant parties, and consulting with legal counsel if necessary.
4. **Employee Notification**: The accused employee will receive a formal written notice detailing the allegations, supporting evidence, and the timeline for responding (usually within three business days).
5. **Employee Response**: The employee will have an opportunity to provide a written response, explanation, or defense. They may also request a meeting with HR to discuss the matter further.
6. **Decision and Action**: Based on findings, HR and management will determine appropriate disciplinary measures. Employees will be informed of the decision in writing, including details of the corrective action and any follow-up requirements.
7. **Documentation**: All disciplinary actions will be documented and stored securely in the employee’s file. Access to such records will be restricted to HR personnel and authorized management.

**Corrective Actions**
The severity of corrective actions will depend on the nature and frequency of the misconduct:
1. **Verbal Warning**: For minor first-time offenses, a verbal warning may be issued. This is documented internally for future reference.
2. **Written Warning**: A written warning is issued for repeat offenses or more serious first-time violations. The employee must acknowledge receipt in writing.
3. **Suspension**: Suspension without pay may be enforced for severe misconduct or repeated violations after prior warnings. The duration will not exceed the limits established by Lebanese Labour Law.
4. **Termination**: For egregious violations, such as theft, harassment, or breaches of confidentiality, termination of employment may be deemed necessary. Termination decisions will comply with all legal notice and severance requirements under Lebanese Labour Law.

**Timelines**
- Incident reporting: Within 5 business days of occurrence.
- Preliminary review: Completed within 3 business days.
- Formal investigation: Initiated within 5 business days and completed within 10 business days.
- Employee response: Submitted within 3 business days of receiving formal notice.
- Decision and action: Finalized within 5 business days of receiving the employee’s response.

**Exceptions**
1. In cases of criminal activity or severe misconduct, the company reserves the right to suspend or terminate employment immediately, without prior warnings, following consultation with legal counsel.
2. If an employee is unable to respond or participate in proceedings due to medical or personal emergencies, timelines may be extended within reasonable limits.
3. Disciplinary action may be waived for minor infractions resolved amicably without escalation.

**Responsibilities**
- **Employees**: Must adhere to company policies, report misconduct, and cooperate during investigations.
- **Managers**: Are responsible for identifying and reporting policy violations, supporting investigations, and enforcing corrective actions.
- **Human Resources**: HR must ensure a fair and impartial process, maintain confidentiality, document proceedings, and comply with Lebanese Labour Law.
- **Employers**: The company is obligated to uphold employee rights, provide clear communication, and ensure legal compliance during disciplinary actions.

**Compliance Notes**
This policy complies with Lebanese Labour Law, particularly provisions related to employment termination, notice periods, and employee rights. All disciplinary actions will be implemented in accordance with legal standards to prevent arbitrary or unjust decisions. Employees retain the right to appeal disciplinary actions through internal processes or authorized legal channels.

By adhering to this policy, inmind.ai fosters a professional and respectful workplace, ensuring accountability while protecting the rights and dignity of all employees.

title: General Workplace Safety Policy
body:
The General Workplace Safety Policy is designed to ensure a safe and healthy working environment for all employees at inmind.ai. This policy aligns with Lebanese Labour Law provisions, particularly clauses addressing workplace safety and employee welfare, and incorporates industry best practices to minimize risks and promote a culture of safety. Ensuring workplace safety is a shared responsibility between the employer and employees, and this policy outlines specific procedures, eligibility criteria, timelines, exceptions, responsibilities, and compliance measures to foster a secure work environment.

**1. Employer Responsibilities**
- The company commits to providing a safe working environment, free from hazards that could result in injury, illness, or damage to property.
- Regular safety audits and inspections will be conducted quarterly to identify potential risks and implement corrective measures.
- All employees will have access to necessary protective equipment (e.g., gloves, helmets, goggles) based on the nature of their roles. The company will provide this equipment at no cost to the employee.
- Comprehensive safety training programs will be organized for all employees during their onboarding process, with mandatory refresher training sessions conducted annually.
- Emergency response protocols, including evacuation procedures, will be clearly communicated and practiced through drills conducted at least twice a year.
- The company will investigate workplace incidents thoroughly within five business days of occurrence, documenting findings and implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
- All safety policies and procedures will be reviewed annually to ensure compliance with Lebanese Labour Law and updates in industry standards.

**2. Employee Responsibilities**
- Employees must adhere strictly to all safety guidelines provided by the company and participate actively in safety training programs.
- Employees are required to use protective equipment provided by the company when performing tasks that pose potential risks.
- Any unsafe conditions, hazards, or incidents must be reported immediately to the employee's direct supervisor or the HR department.
- Employees must familiarize themselves with emergency response protocols and actively participate in drills and related activities.
- Smoking, alcohol consumption, and the use of illegal substances are strictly prohibited within company premises. Non-compliance may result in disciplinary action, including termination, in accordance with Lebanese Labour Law.
- Employees must cooperate fully with investigations into workplace incidents and follow any corrective measures implemented.

**3. Eligibility Criteria**
- This policy applies to all employees, regardless of role, contract type, or seniority, including full-time, part-time, and temporary workers.
- External contractors, freelancers, or visitors to the premises must also adhere to the company’s safety guidelines while on-site. These individuals will be briefed on relevant protocols before commencing work or entering restricted areas.

**4. Procedures**
- **Reporting Unsafe Conditions:** Employees should report unsafe conditions or hazards to their supervisor or HR immediately. Reports can be made verbally or in writing, and anonymous reporting options are available via the company’s safety hotline or email.
- **Incident Reporting and Investigation:** In the event of an accident or near-miss incident, employees must notify their supervisor within 24 hours. The company will initiate an investigation within 48 hours, with a final report and recommended corrective actions completed within five business days.
- **Emergency Response:** Employees must follow the established emergency response protocols, which are detailed in the Employee Handbook and displayed in key areas around the workplace. These protocols include evacuation routes, assembly points, and contact information for emergency responders.
- **Safety Training and Drills:** All employees will undergo initial safety training during onboarding, with additional role-specific training provided as needed. Participation in periodic safety drills is mandatory.

**5. Timelines**
- Safety audits: Conducted quarterly.
- Safety training: Initial training during onboarding, with annual refresher sessions.
- Emergency drills: Conducted biannually (every six months).
- Investigation of incidents: Initiated within 48 hours of reporting, with a final report submitted within five business days.

**6. Exceptions**
- Employees with documented medical conditions that prevent the use of specific protective equipment must submit medical certification to HR. Where possible, reasonable accommodations will be made.
- In extreme circumstances, such as natural disasters or other emergencies outside the company’s control, certain safety procedures may be adjusted to prioritize immediate employee safety.
- Visitors or external contractors refusing to comply with safety guidelines may be denied access to the premises.

**7. Compliance and Disciplinary Action**
- Non-compliance with this policy, including failure to follow safety guidelines, report hazards, or use protective equipment, may result in disciplinary action in accordance with the company’s Disciplinary Policy and Lebanese Labour Law.
- Severe violations, such as intentional disregard for safety measures or engaging in prohibited activities (e.g., substance use on company premises), may lead to immediate termination.

**8. Monitoring and Review**
- The HR department, in collaboration with the Safety Committee, will monitor the implementation of this policy and ensure compliance. Annual reviews will be conducted to update the policy as needed, reflecting changes in Lebanese Labour Law or industry standards.

**9. Fostering a Culture of Safety**
This policy underscores the company’s commitment to prioritizing employee welfare and operational safety. Employees are encouraged to actively contribute to a safe workplace by being vigilant, reporting concerns promptly, and supporting their colleagues in adhering to safety protocols. By fostering a culture of accountability and shared responsibility, inmind.ai aims to create a workplace where safety is not only a priority but a core value.

title: Performance Review Policy
body:
### Purpose
This Performance Review Policy outlines the standards, procedures, and responsibilities associated with employee performance evaluations at inmind.ai. This policy ensures compliance with Lebanese Labour Law, fosters a culture of continuous improvement, and promotes employee development while maintaining fairness and transparency.

### Scope
This policy applies to all employees of inmind.ai, regardless of position, department, or contract type (permanent, part-time, or fixed-term), unless otherwise stated in the employment agreement. 

### Objectives
1. Assess employee performance against defined goals and competencies.
2. Identify areas of excellence and areas requiring improvement.
3. Facilitate open communication between employees and supervisors.
4. Promote career development and professional growth.
5. Align individual goals with organizational objectives.

### Performance Review Cycle
At inmind.ai, a formal performance review is conducted annually, with a mid-year check-in to assess progress and provide feedback. Additional reviews may be conducted in the following cases:
1. At the end of a probationary period (refer to the Probationary Period Policy).
2. After significant role changes or promotions.
3. Upon an employee’s request, subject to manager approval.

### Eligibility Criteria
1. All full-time and part-time employees are subject to performance reviews.
2. Employees on probation will receive a review at the end of their probationary period.
3. Employees on extended leave (e.g., maternity leave, sick leave) will have their reviews deferred until they return to work and have had sufficient time (minimum one month) to demonstrate performance.

### Review Process
#### 1. Setting Goals and Expectations:
- At the beginning of the performance cycle, managers and employees will collaboratively set SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) goals.
- Performance expectations, including key performance indicators (KPIs) and behavioral competencies, will be clearly outlined and documented.

#### 2. Ongoing Feedback:
- Managers are encouraged to provide regular feedback throughout the year to address performance issues promptly and recognize achievements.
- Employees are encouraged to actively seek feedback to enhance their performance.

#### 3. Self-Assessment:
- Prior to the formal review meeting, employees will complete a self-assessment form, reflecting on their accomplishments, challenges, and development needs.

#### 4. Manager Evaluation:
- Managers will evaluate employee performance based on the following:
  a. Achievement of pre-defined goals.
  b. Demonstration of organizational values and competencies.
  c. Quality, quantity, and timeliness of work.
  d. Feedback from relevant stakeholders (clients, peers, etc.).
  e. Compliance with company policies and procedures.

#### 5. Review Meeting:
- A performance review meeting will be scheduled at a mutually agreed time.
- The manager and employee will discuss the self-assessment, manager evaluation, and any other relevant feedback.
- Strengths, areas for improvement, and development opportunities will be identified.
- The employee will be given an opportunity to raise concerns or suggest adjustments.

#### 6. Development Plan:
- Based on the review, a personalized development plan will be created, outlining:
  a. Specific training or skill development needs.
  b. Opportunities for career progression.
  c. Any corrective actions required to address performance gaps.

#### 7. Documentation:
- The completed performance review form will be signed by both the manager and the employee.
- A copy will be provided to the employee, and the original will be securely stored in the employee’s HR file.

### Performance Ratings
The following rating scale will be used during the evaluation process:
1. **Exceeds Expectations:** Consistently exceeds performance standards in all areas.
2. **Meets Expectations:** Consistently meets performance standards.
3. **Needs Improvement:** Meets some performance standards but requires improvement in specific areas.
4. **Does Not Meet Expectations:** Fails to meet performance standards in most areas.

### Responsibilities
#### HR Department:
1. Develop and maintain performance review templates and tools.
2. Provide training to managers and employees on the performance review process.
3. Ensure timely scheduling and completion of reviews.
4. Maintain confidentiality of performance review records.

#### Managers:
1. Clearly communicate performance expectations and provide ongoing feedback.
2. Conduct fair and unbiased evaluations based on objective criteria.
3. Document performance discussions and development plans accurately.
4. Support employees in achieving their development goals.

#### Employees:
1. Actively participate in the performance review process.
2. Complete self-assessments honestly and thoroughly.
3. Implement agreed-upon development plans and seek assistance when needed.

### Exceptions and Special Circumstances
1. Employees on extended leave will have their reviews deferred as stated in the Eligibility Criteria.
2. In cases where an employee’s performance is deteriorating significantly, an interim review may be conducted to address issues and create an improvement plan.
3. Employees undergoing disciplinary action may be subject to a specialized performance improvement plan (PIP) instead of the standard review process.

### Confidentiality
All performance review discussions, forms, and related documents are confidential and accessible only to the employee, the manager, HR, and authorized personnel. Breaches of confidentiality may lead to disciplinary action.

### Appeals
If an employee disagrees with their performance evaluation, they may:
1. Discuss their concerns with their manager within five business days of receiving the review.
2. If unresolved, escalate the matter to the HR department for mediation.
3. Submit a formal appeal in writing, including detailed reasons for the disagreement.

### Compliance with Lebanese Labour Law
This policy complies with Article 50 of the Lebanese Labour Law, which emphasizes the importance of fair treatment in performance-related matters. Employees have the right to contest performance reviews if they believe the process was unfair or biased.

### Policy Review and Updates
This policy will be reviewed annually by the HR department to ensure its relevance and alignment with organizational goals and legal requirements. Updates will be communicated to all employees in writing.

### Effective Date
This policy is effective as of the date of its publication and supersedes all previous performance review policies.

By adhering to this policy, inmind.ai aims to create a fair and consistent performance management process that fosters employee growth and organizational success.

title: Employee Onboarding Policy
body:
### Employee Onboarding Policy

#### 1. Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to outline the onboarding process at inmind.ai to ensure new hires are effectively integrated into the company’s culture, operations, and compliance with Lebanese Labour Law. This policy establishes procedures, responsibilities, and expectations to facilitate a smooth transition for employees starting their roles.

#### 2. Scope
This policy applies to all newly hired employees at inmind.ai, including full-time, part-time, temporary, and contractual employees.

#### 3. Objectives
- To provide new employees with the tools and resources necessary for success in their roles.
- To ensure legal compliance with Lebanese Labour Law, including proper registration with the National Social Security Fund (NSSF).
- To foster a welcoming and inclusive workplace culture.
- To provide clarity on job responsibilities, performance expectations, and company policies.

#### 4. Pre-Onboarding Procedures

4.1 **Offer Letter and Employment Contract**
- The Human Resources (HR) department is responsible for issuing a formal offer letter and employment contract to the selected candidate. These documents must clearly outline the terms of employment, including job title, salary, benefits, probationary period, and any other relevant conditions.
- Candidates must sign and return the offer letter and contract within five (5) business days of receipt.

4.2 **Pre-Employment Documentation**
- The candidate must provide the following documents before their first day of employment:
  - Valid ID or passport.
  - Social security number for NSSF registration.
  - Copies of academic certificates and professional qualifications.
  - Bank account details for salary transfers.
  - Any other documents requested by HR.
- HR will verify the authenticity of these documents and ensure compliance with Lebanese Labour Law.

4.3 **Workspace and Equipment Preparation**
- The IT and Facilities departments are responsible for preparing the employee’s workspace and equipment, including laptops, access cards, and email accounts. This must be completed at least two (2) business days before the employee’s start date.

#### 5. Day One Onboarding

5.1 **Welcome Session**
- On the first day, the HR department will conduct a welcome session to introduce the new employee to the company’s mission, vision, values, and organizational structure.
- The session will also include an overview of key policies, including:
  - Code of Conduct.
  - Anti-Harassment Policy.
  - Health and Safety Guidelines.

5.2 **Team Introduction**
- The new employee’s manager will introduce them to their team and explain the team’s structure and key responsibilities.
- A designated team member may be assigned as a “buddy” to assist the new employee during their first month.

5.3 **NSSF Registration and Legal Compliance**
- HR will ensure the employee is registered with the NSSF within fifteen (15) days of starting their employment, as mandated by Lebanese Labour Law.
- A copy of the NSSF registration confirmation will be provided to the employee.

#### 6. Onboarding During the First Month

6.1 **Training and Development**
- The employee will undergo role-specific training during the first month, which may include:
  - Technical training.
  - Software and tools orientation.
  - Compliance training on Lebanese Labour Law and company policies.
- Managers are responsible for creating a training schedule tailored to the employee’s role.

6.2 **Performance Goals and Expectations**
- Within the first week, the manager will meet with the employee to:
  - Set performance goals for the probationary period.
  - Explain key performance indicators (KPIs) and evaluation criteria.
- The manager will provide a written summary of these goals to the employee and HR.

6.3 **Probation Period Review**
- All new employees are subject to a three-month probationary period, in accordance with Lebanese Labour Law.
- During the probationary period:
  - Managers must conduct bi-weekly check-ins with the employee to provide feedback.
  - Employees are encouraged to discuss any challenges or concerns.
- At the end of the probationary period, a formal evaluation will determine whether the employee will be confirmed in their role.

#### 7. Responsibilities

7.1 **HR Department**
- Coordinate all aspects of the onboarding process.
- Ensure compliance with Lebanese Labour Law, including timely NSSF registration.
- Provide support to both the new employee and their manager during the onboarding process.

7.2 **Managers**
- Prepare training schedules and set performance expectations.
- Provide regular feedback and support to the new employee.
- Facilitate team introductions and integration.

7.3 **New Employees**
- Complete all required pre-employment paperwork and provide necessary documentation.
- Actively participate in training and onboarding sessions.
- Seek clarification on policies, procedures, or job responsibilities as needed.

#### 8. Exceptions
- Exceptions to any aspect of this policy must be approved in writing by the HR Manager.
- Temporary employees may have a modified onboarding process, subject to the terms of their contract.
- Employees starting remotely may have virtual onboarding sessions, with physical documentation to be completed at the first in-person opportunity.

#### 9. Policy Review
This policy will be reviewed annually to ensure compliance with Lebanese Labour Law and alignment with company objectives. Changes to the policy will be communicated to all employees in a timely manner.

#### 10. Enforcement
Failure to adhere to the onboarding policy may result in delays in employment processes or disciplinary action, depending on the severity of the non-compliance. Managers and HR are responsible for ensuring the policy is implemented fairly and consistently.

#### 11. Effective Date
This policy is effective immediately and supersedes any previous onboarding guidelines or procedures.

title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
body:
### Purpose
This Expense Reimbursement Policy provides clear guidelines and procedures for employees of inmind.ai to claim reimbursement for business-related expenses, in compliance with Lebanese Labour Law and industry best practices. The policy ensures fairness, transparency, and accountability in the management of company resources.

### Scope
This policy applies to all employees of inmind.ai, including full-time, part-time, and contract staff, who incur expenses while conducting legitimate business activities for the company. This includes, but is not limited to, transportation, accommodation, meals, office supplies, and other work-related expenditures.

### Eligibility Criteria
1. **Authorized Expenses**: Employees are eligible to claim reimbursement for expenses that are:
   - Necessary and directly related to the performance of their duties.
   - Pre-approved by their direct supervisor or department head, where applicable.
   - Incurred while adhering to the company’s travel and expenditure guidelines.

2. **Employee Categories**: This policy covers the following categories of employees:
   - Full-time employees.
   - Part-time employees, provided the expenses are linked to their assigned tasks.
   - Contractual staff, contingent upon the terms outlined in their contract.

3. **Non-Reimbursable Expenses**: The following are examples of expenses that are not eligible for reimbursement:
   - Personal expenses unrelated to business activities.
   - Fines, penalties, or traffic violations incurred during business trips.
   - Alcoholic beverages unless consumed during official business events and pre-approved.
   - Loss of personal property.

### General Guidelines
1. **Pre-Approval Requirement**: Employees must obtain prior written approval for all major expenditures exceeding $500 (or its equivalent in Lebanese Pounds) from their department head or a designated manager.

2. **Documentation Requirements**: Employees must provide detailed and accurate documentation for all expenses, including:
   - Original receipts or invoices clearly showing the amount, date, and nature of the expense.
   - For mileage claims, a log with the date, purpose of the trip, starting location, destination, and kilometers traveled.
   - For travel expenses, boarding passes and hotel bills must be attached.

3. **Timeliness of Claims**: Claims for reimbursement must be submitted within 30 calendar days from the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted after this period may only be considered under exceptional circumstances approved by the HR Department.

4. **Exchange Rate Policy**: For expenses incurred in foreign currencies, employees must provide proof of the exchange rate used (e.g., credit card statement or official exchange rate on the date of the transaction). The company will use the official exchange rate for reimbursement purposes.

### Reimbursement Process
1. **Submission of Claims**:
   - Employees must complete the Expense Reimbursement Form, available on the company’s HR portal.
   - Attach all required supporting documentation to the form.
   - Submit the completed form to their immediate supervisor for initial review and approval.

2. **Supervisor Review**:
   - The supervisor must review the accuracy and legitimacy of the expense claims.
   - Once approved, the supervisor forwards the claim to the Finance Department for processing.

3. **Finance Department Review**:
   - The Finance Department verifies the submitted documentation and ensures compliance with this policy.
   - Approved claims are processed for payment within 10 business days from the date of submission to the Finance Department.

4. **Payment of Reimbursement**:
   - Reimbursements are made via bank transfer to the employee’s registered bank account.
   - Employees will receive a notification email once the reimbursement is processed.

### Exceptions
1. **Emergency Expenses**: In cases of emergency where prior approval is not possible, employees must notify their direct supervisor within 24 hours of incurring the expense. The supervisor must confirm the necessity and legitimacy of the expense retrospectively.

2. **Lost or Missing Receipts**:
   - If an employee is unable to provide a receipt for a legitimate expense, they must complete a Missing Receipt Declaration Form and provide a detailed explanation of the expense.
   - Approval of such claims is at the sole discretion of the Finance Department and may require additional authorization from senior management.

3. **Advance Payments**:
   - In certain cases, employees may request an advance payment for anticipated business expenses. Such requests must be submitted to the Finance Department at least 5 business days before the funds are required.
   - Employees who receive advance payments are required to submit a detailed expense report and return any unused funds within 15 days of completing the activity.

### Employee Responsibilities
1. Employees are responsible for:
   - Ensuring that all expenses are reasonable, necessary, and directly related to company business.
   - Obtaining and retaining original receipts and documentation for all expenses.
   - Submitting claims accurately and in a timely manner.
   - Adhering to this policy and any additional guidelines issued by their department.

2. Non-compliance with this policy may result in:
   - Denial of reimbursement claims.
   - Disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment, in cases of intentional misrepresentation or fraud.

### Employer Responsibilities
1. inmind.ai is committed to:
   - Providing clear guidelines and training to employees on the reimbursement process.
   - Processing reimbursement claims in a timely and accurate manner.
   - Maintaining transparency and fairness in the evaluation and approval of claims.
   - Ensuring compliance with Lebanese Labour Law and applicable tax regulations.

### Review and Amendments
This policy will be reviewed annually by the HR and Finance Departments to ensure it remains relevant and compliant with Lebanese Labour Law and the company’s operational needs. Any amendments to this policy will be communicated to employees in writing.

### Contact Information
For questions or clarifications regarding this policy, employees should contact the HR Department at hr@inmind.ai or the Finance Department at finance@inmind.ai.

### Acknowledgment
Employees must acknowledge their understanding and acceptance of this policy by signing the Expense Reimbursement Policy Acknowledgment Form, available on the HR portal. Failure to provide acknowledgment does not exempt employees from adhering to the policy.
